concept:
Refactoring the Theme Injector (Zero-CPU Upgrade) 2026-06-20 firefox, css, performance, gpu, intel-hd-4000, theme, optimization, zero-cpu, hardware-acceleration, theme_injector
The existing `theme_injector.py` script was found to contain outdated CSS payloads that violate the Zero-CPU doctrine. It relies heavily on layout-thrashing properties (`border`, `box-shadow` on hover, and heavy background images). This concept outlines the plan to rewrite the injector script's payload to conform to our Intel HD 4000 hardware acceleration constraints.
<findings> <finding name="CPU-Killing CSS Found"> The old CSS in `theme_injector.py` was forcing the CPU to recalculate the box model (reflows) on every hover/click interaction. Examples include using `border` instead of `outline`, and `box-shadow` which is expensive to blend. </finding> <finding name="Background Compositing Overhead"> The `nebula.jpg` background applied to `#navigator-toolbox` was causing massive compositing overhead on the UI thread. </finding> </findings>
<the_plan> <step id="1" name="Rewrite Injector Script"> Replace the `css_content` block in `theme_injector.py`. Swap all `border` properties for `outline` (which lives purely on the GPU). Remove heavy background compositing on the toolbar. </step> <step id="2" name="Implement Hardware Acceleration Rules"> Explicitly add `will-change: transform` and `contain: strict` to interactive elements like tabs and the URL bar to pre-promote them to GPU compositor layers. Ensure all animations strictly use `transform` and `opacity`. </step> <step id="3" name="Execute and Bake"> Run the updated injector script to overwrite the core fallback theme files in the source tree. Run a final `./mach build` to bake the highly-optimized, GPU-accelerated theme directly into the `libxul.so` binary. </step> </the_plan>
